recipes.name: Cashew Chicken with Water Chestnuts
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast meat - cut into strips
1 (8 ounce) can sliced water chestnuts, drained

steps.text: Dissolve cornstarch in chicken broth in a bowl; stir in soy sauce, ginger, and hot sauce. Set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add chicken; cook and stir until no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate; set aside.

Add remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the wok. Add onion, bell pepper, and water chestnuts; cook and stir until onion has softened and water chestnuts are hot, about 5 minutes. Stir reserved sauce to redistribute cornstarch; stir into the wok. Bring to a boil. Add reserved chicken; stir until sauce thickens and chicken is hot. Sprinkle with cashews.

raw_recipe.headline: Cashew Chicken with Water Chestnuts
raw_recipe.description: This stir-fry recipe includes cashews, chicken, water chestnuts, bell pepper, onion, ground ginger, hot pepper sauce, soy sauce, and chicken broth.

review.reviewBody: This was wonderful! It tasted better than the take-out we get! I did make a few minor changes. I cooked my chicken in olive oil with a dash of sesame oil, added 2 celery stalks to the veggies, added 1 tsp. minced garlic, and subbed 3/4 tsp. fresh grated ginger for the ground ginger. This is the best Chinese food recipe we have tried yet from this site. Thanks Tricia!!

This is a very good recipe as written. As written, I rate this a 4. With my tweaks I give it 5. My changes: substitute 1 tablespoon seame oil for one tbsp of vegetable oil. Add 1 clove of minced garlic. Marinate the chicken in the sauce for 15 minutes before cooking. Lastly, at the end of the cooking time, add 1 tbsp hoisin sauce. This is a great recipe, and I will make it again both ways! My family loves it. One last thing: I used about half of the cornstarch. Way too thick with 2 tablespoons. Also, for an interesting variation, try adding a can of pineapple chunks toward the end of the cooking!

This was great! I used 2 teaspoons of hoisin sauce instead of hot sauce and added broccoli,mushrooms and celery. I also doubled the sauce and toasted the cashews as I was cooking the vege's. :) I cooked the chicken in 1/4 cup of chicken broth,sesame seeds and a tish of soy sauce. I've made this 3 or 4 times, this time I marinated the chicken in the soy mixture then cooked the chicken in the oil and toasted the cashews toward the end. Removed the chicken and cashews and stir fried the veges.When slightly cooked I added corn starch to the remaining marinade, added that to the veges and steamed for a few minutes while veges finished cooking. I decided, on a whim to add a teaspoon of honey and OMG! so good!

Very good! I used 1 cup of chicken broth, but did not add the cornstarch to that. After cooking the onions, green pepper and chicken (together) in sesame oil, I added in a can of cut baby corn and the water chestnuts. I then added the sauce, which I added some minced garlic to, and allowed that to simmer a few minutes. I then thickened it to where I wanted it w/ a cornstrch/water slurry and added in the cashews. This was delicious and had a nice balance of flavors. Super simple and something that I would def make again! Thanks for sharing. :)

This is a good starter recipe. I added doubled the sauce (except the cornstarch), added the 2 tbls hoisin recommended by others, a tsp of 5 spice, and a dash of thai hot chili-garlic sauce. Cooked the chicken in sesame oil. This came out delicious and it's a keeper!

Excellent recipe. Added fresh ginger and oyster sauce (2 T of soy sauce and 1 T of oyster) and fresh garlic for personal tastes. Also added 2 stalks of celery to up the veggies. Sprinkled green onion on top when served. Delicious!

I automatically replaced the ground ginger with finely minced ginger root (approx. a Tbsp.), and stir fried that with the chicken. I replaced the green pepper with red pepper (much tastier). I found that there wasn't enough sauce, and it was too thick, so next time I would use more chicken broth (maybe about a cup, or slightly more). Don't be afraid to add the hot sauce - it doesn't turn out that hot. Next time I might stir in the cashews at the end, rather than sprinkling them on. I'm also going to try adding a dash of sesame oil, as per other reviewers, and some minced garlic and celery to the recipe. Tweaking a little never hurts! Definitely a good recipe!

I substituted Red bell pepper for Green, added few stalks of chopped celery and used chicken thighs instead of breast meat. Also I marinated the sliced thighs with seasoning salt and cooking wine for an hour before cooking. Used roasted cashew nuts. It turns out very flavorful and colorful.
Cook chicken with ginger, garlic, red pepper flake. Leave out the onions, do large sliced bell pepper and sugar snap peas. Double the hot sauce. And I think it needs a tsp of honey.

Big hit with family. Didn't have bell pepper or water chestnuts, so used asparagus and carrots. Used tamarin instead of soy sauce to make it gluten free. Used siriacha sauce for the hot sauce. Was delicious and came together quickly. Nice thick sauce, with crisp veggies. The sauce wasn't spicy at all. I think the 1/2 t of hot sauce is just to give depth to the recipe. Big winner at our house.
I made this for dinner for myself last night, and it was delicious!! Before adding the cornstarch mixture to the sautéed veggies, I added the cashews and cooked them for a few minutes.

I left out the ginger because of family allergies, but definitely think it would make this dish better. I do think the cornstarch/liquid ratio is off. I added a lot of extra broth at the end so I would have a sauce instead of very thick coating around the chicken and vegetables. / Update: When I made this a second time, I added some oyster sauce. That was definitely helpful to the flavor profile.

Followed the recipe as-is, and it was better than average, as my rating reflects. Two vegetable swaps I made the 2nd time through helped tremendously: Red bell pepper replacing green, and bamboo shoots + garlic replacing onion. Excellent recipe either way, and it's one I reuse!
Nice

Very easy and tasty. I didn’t have the pepper sauce so I used a bit of cayenne and omitted the green pepper. This recipe is a great base and you can add water chestnuts, bamboo shoots, vegetables. I did all of the above and needed no side dishes. So, so yummy ??
Loved this! I didn’t have hot pepper sauce so I just sprinkled some red pepper flakes and used one of those frozen bags of mixed stir fry vegetables. Really tasty and light for Chinese
I thought this recipe might turn out bland, but it was amazingly delicious!!! I look forward to making it again
Delicious.
Pretty simple to throw together using just one pan. If you have a rice cooker it's even quicker. All hail the rice cooker.

It was ok, not super, just ok. When the sauce hit the pan it thickened immediately, so there was some split second timing going on there; hard for me as I'm a beginner. I also thought the sauce could have benefitted from some seasoning
